purpose: Reliability-hardening pass fixing audit issue #300 (api-data-fetching): reconstructs deep/old review-comment threads via a single-pass paginated walk with a by-id fallback and cycle guards, adds a bounded window plus by-id fallback for issue-comment conversation context, tracks failed file batches with a 'Partial review' banner, keys the lessons cache by the file-path set, makes audit-issue dedup fail-open, honors sort direction in the GitLab adapter, threads AbortSignal through the API helpers, and adds an authenticated opencode release lookup with an anonymous fallback.
riskRationale: No critical defects and all test suites (781 lib + 14 action + 18 app), typecheck, and lint pass. Risk is medium because the conversation-context fix relies on GitHub's per-issue comments endpoint honoring direction:desc, which it does not (the parameter is silently ignored and comments are always returned ascending), so @mention context is still lost or chronologically inverted on the primary platform; the review-comment gatherer and reply-flow thread reconstruction also fetch their windows oldest-first, hurting busy PRs; and the ambient token is still transmitted to api.github.com for a public cross-repo release lookup. All of these are small, localized fixes with no breaking changes.

text: A well-structured, well-tested resilience pass: cycle guards in every in_reply_to_id walk, a keyed lessons cache, failedBatches surfaced as a 'Partial review' banner, fail-open audit dedup, GitLab sort-direction mapping, and live AbortSignal plumbing are all solid improvements. The main gap is that the issue-comment conversation window assumes GitHub returns comments newest-first (direction:'desc'), but the per-issue comments endpoint ignores that parameter and returns ascending — so the very context the PR was meant to provide is still lost on GitHub, and the review-comment gatherer/reply flow repeat the same oldest-first window mistake on busy PRs.

reasoning: One important correctness bug remains: gatherIssueCommentThread (conversation.ts:353) relies on a GitHub API ordering behavior the endpoint does not provide, silently losing or inverting @mention conversation context on the primary platform; gatherReviewCommentThread (conversation.ts:202) has the same oldest-first window on busy PRs, and setupOpenCode still transmits the ambient token to api.github.com for a public cross-repo lookup (opencode.ts:128). All remaining important fixes are small and localized (ordering-aware slice, direction flip, token gating), so an automated agent can address them safely.

message: Keying the lessons cache by the sorted, deduplicated file-path set is a correct bug fix: previously lessons for one file set were silently reused for any other file set within the 60s TTL, serving mismatched learning context. It also aligns the lessons cache with the existing mcpDocsCache keying pattern.

failedBatches is propagated into the final ReviewResult and survives both the synthesis-fallback branch and the linter-dedup rebuild via the conditional spread, and review-body.ts renders it as a prominent 'Partial review' banner so consumers and the autofix loop can tell findings may be incomplete.

The single-pass review-comment thread reconstruction converts the inherently sequential N+1 direct-fetch walk into one bounded fetch; the needsDirectWalk fallback starts from the deepest found ancestor and resolves in-window comments from the map (never re-fetching or duplicating), and the walked/walkedMissing cycle guards terminate malformed chains. Regression tests guard the [1,2,2,3] duplicate-ID and cyclic-chain cases.

The in_reply_to_id chain walk indexes comments into a Map for O(1) lookups, guards cyclic chains with a visited set, preserves diff_hunk/filePath from direct fetches, and returns a partially gathered chain instead of dropping the whole conversation when a single ancestor fetch fails.

Paginate now maps the GitHub-style direction option to order_by=created_at&sort, fixing the cross-platform ordering mismatch where the asc/desc assumptions in conversation.ts were silently reversed on GitLab (which returns notes newest-first by default). Covered by new ascending/descending paginate tests.

The existing-issue search is now fail-open: on a pagination failure the action warns and creates the issue (accepting a rare duplicate) so findings are never silently dropped, while core.setFailed is reserved for the genuine case where the issue write itself fails. The integration suite verifies the update-instead-of-duplicate path.

The authenticated release lookup degrades gracefully: on 401/403/404 the request is retried anonymously so GitLab CI (a non-GitHub token sent to api.github.com) fails fast and recovers without aborting setup, and removing 403 from retryableStatuses avoids burning three backoff retries on a deterministic rejection. Note the token is still transmitted on the first attempt — see the important issue below.

gatherIssueCommentThread requests the issue-comment window with direction:'desc', but GitHub's per-issue comments endpoint (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}/comments) documents only since/per_page/page and does not support sort/direction — the parameter is silently ignored and comments are always returned ascending by ID (verified against GitHub REST docs). Consequence on GitHub: on PRs with more than 500 issue comments the freshly-posted trigger is outside the 5-page window, so triggerIdx === -1 and the by-id fallback yields only [trigger] with zero preceding context; on smaller PRs the trigger IS in-window but at the END (ascending), so slice(triggerIdx, triggerIdx+6).reverse() selects comments posted AFTER the trigger and reverses them into chronologically inverted context. The new test (conversation.test.ts:190) mocks a newest-first payload GitHub can never return, so it passes without exercising the real API contract. GitLab works only because gitlab-adapter maps direction to order_by/sort.
suggestion: Fetch in ascending order (GitHub's default; gitlab-adapter also honors 'asc') and slice the 5 comments preceding the trigger instead of reversing a newest-first window. Update the test to feed an ascending array as GitHub actually returns.

message: gatherReviewCommentThread fetches the review-comment window oldest-first (direction:'asc', perPage 100, maxPages 5 = the 500 OLDEST review comments). An @mention trigger is freshly posted, so on any PR with more than 500 review comments it is never in the window: the trigger and every ancestor are recovered by N+1 sequential getReviewComment calls (conversation.ts:253-267), and the subtree expansion (conversation.ts:286-297) only scans the old window so recent sibling/nested replies are silently omitted — losing exactly the recent context this PR aims to preserve. This is the same class of busy-PR regression already fixed for the issue-comment gatherer (desc, conversation.ts:353) but missed here.
suggestion: Flip the window to newest-first (direction:'desc') — unlike the issue-comments endpoint, the review-comments endpoint (GET /pulls/{n}/comments) does support sort/direction — so recent triggers and their replies land in-window. Ordering is already normalized by the explicit id sort at conversation.ts:301 and the chain walk is order-independent via the byId map, so the flip is safe.

message: setupOpenCode still sends the ambient GITHUB_TOKEN || INPUT_GITHUB_TOKEN as an Authorization bearer header to api.github.com for the public, cross-repo anomalyco/opencode release lookup where anonymous access succeeds. In GitLab CI, INPUT_GITHUB_TOKEN frequently holds a non-GitHub credential that then gets transmitted to GitHub's infrastructure; a repo-scoped Actions token is likewise sent despite being unable to authorize a cross-repo lookup. The 401/403/404 anonymous fallback fixes the failure mode but not the unnecessary credential transmission (least-privilege), and a 429/5xx on the authenticated attempt still burns the backoff retries first.
suggestion: Only attach the ambient token when the runtime is GitHub Actions where it is guaranteed to be a GitHub credential; outside Actions, call the public endpoint anonymously so the token is never transmitted.

message: getReviewCommentThread's single-pass reconstruction also fetches the window oldest-first (direction:'asc', perPage 100, maxPages 10 = the 1000 OLDEST review comments). On PRs with more than 1000 review comments the just-replied-to trigger is out of window, so the reply flow pays for up to 10 paginated fetches AND then falls back to the fully sequential by-id chain walk (walkChainById, github.ts:1049-1057) — strictly more work than the pre-PR behavior for the reply path. Since the chain is rebuilt from commentById and chainIds is root-first by construction, a desc window keeps recent triggers in the single pass and reserves the by-id walk for genuinely old ancestors.
suggestion: Fetch the getReviewCommentThread window with direction:'desc' so recent reply triggers are found in the single pass, avoiding both the wasted page fetches and the N+1 chain walk on busy PRs.

message: The AbortSignal plumbing remains partial in GitHubHelper: getReviewCommentThread has no signal parameter, and the direct-fetch ancestor walks — the needsDirectWalk branch (github.ts:966) and walkChainById (github.ts:1054) — call getReviewComment(0, ancestorId) without forwarding any signal, so a cancelled reply webhook cannot abort these sequential chain walks. Only the paginated list path receives a signal, so cancellation is inconsistently applied.
suggestion: Accept an optional signal in getReviewCommentThread and forward it to every getReviewComment and listReviewComments call so both the paginated list and the direct-fetch chain walks are cancellable.

message: Error handling is inconsistent between the two dedup branches: a failed postOrUpdateComment on an existing issue only logs a warning (audit.ts:162-164) and leaves the workflow green, while the create branch calls core.setFailed. A silent update failure leaves stale audit findings with no signal to the user.
suggestion: Mirror the create branch: call core.setFailed('Audit issue tracking failed — could not update issue') in the update catch so a failed update is surfaced.

message: The fail-open behavior (existingIssueNumber = undefined on search failure) means that during a persistent search outage every workflow run creates a brand-new audit issue — duplicates accumulate over time, whereas the previous behavior skipped creation. The tradeoff is documented, but unbounded duplicate creation should be limited.
suggestion: Add a guard so the fail-open create path only runs once per category per time window, or record the last issue number and attempt dedup against it on the next run.

message: When the trigger is older than the window, the single gh.getIssueComment by-id fetch sits inside the outer try; if it fails (transient 500, rate limit, deleted comment), the catch returns { thread: [] } and handleConversation silently skips the user's @mention with no response (conversation.ts:88-91) — the one failure path the partial-chain resilience does not cover.
suggestion: Catch the by-id trigger fetch separately and return the minimal thread only when it succeeds; on failure log a warning and still proceed with an empty thread (or fall back to the newest window comments) so the @mention is answered rather than dropped.

message: The subtree expansion loop is O(n²) worst case: while(changed) rescans all rawComments (up to 500) on every iteration, and in a pathological thread where each pass adds only one comment it can iterate ~n times (~250k iterations per @mention). A single-pass BFS seeded with the chain IDs and indexed by in_reply_to_id would be O(n).
suggestion: Replace the repeated full scans with a queue-based breadth-first traversal over rawComments indexed by in_reply_to_id.

message: getReviewCommentThread (github.ts:883-1061) and conversation.ts gatherReviewCommentThread (186-319) now implement near-identical in_reply_to_id chain walking with cycle guards, by-id fallbacks, and path/diffHunk anchoring, but with divergent window bounds (maxPages 10 vs 5) and slightly different edge handling — a bug fixed in one will likely be missed in the other.
suggestion: Extract the shared chain-walk/subtree logic into a lib helper operating on the PlatformAdapter interface and have both call sites consume it with their respective window bounds as parameters.

message: The gatherIssueCommentThread test feeds a pre-sorted newest-first mock array (ids 10..1), so it only validates the slice arithmetic against an ordering the real GitHub issue-comments endpoint can never produce (it ignores direction and returns ascending) — the important ordering bug at conversation.ts:353 is never exercised.
suggestion: Add a companion test passing an ascending (oldest-first) array as GitHub actually returns and assert the preceding comments are selected; this would have caught the ordering bug.

message: A 404 from the authenticated release lookup is treated as an auth failure and retried anonymously, but 404 can also mean the requested version tag does not exist (e.g. setupOpenCode('v9.9.9')). The anonymous retry returns the same 404 body, which has no assets, so release.assets.find(...) at opencode.ts:172 throws a confusing TypeError instead of a clear 'release/tag not found' error.
suggestion: After the anonymous fallback, check release.assets presence (or the GitHub 404 body) and throw a clear error naming the tag so setup failures are diagnosable.
